en: Puggalapaññatti Niddesa 9. Exposition of the Designation of Nine Types of Persons
And what kind of person is a perfectly enlightened one (sammāsambuddha)?
Here, a certain person, regarding teachings not heard before, awakens to the truths by himself and attains therein omniscience and mastery over the powers.
This is called a person who is a perfectly enlightened one.
And what kind of person is a *paccekasambuddha* (a solitary enlightened one)?
Here, a certain person, regarding teachings not heard before, personally awakens to the Truths; yet he does not attain omniscience therein, nor mastery over the powers (*bala*).
This is called a person who is a *paccekasambuddha*.
And what is the person liberated in both ways?
Here, a certain person dwells having personally realized the eight liberations with the body, and having seen with wisdom, his taints are utterly destroyed.
This is called the person liberated in both ways.
And what kind of person is one liberated by wisdom?
Here, a certain person does not dwell having personally realized the eight liberations with the body, yet through seeing with wisdom, his taints are utterly destroyed.
This person is called one liberated by wisdom.
And what kind of person is a body-witness (kāyasakkhī)?
Here, a certain person dwells having personally experienced the eight liberations with the body; and having seen with wisdom, some of his taints are completely destroyed.
This is called a person who is a body-witness.
And what is the person who has attained through vision?
Here, a certain person understands as it really is: "This is suffering" ... [and so on] ...

"This is the practice leading to the cessation of suffering. The teachings proclaimed by the Tathāgata have been clearly seen and mastered by his wisdom; and having seen with wisdom, some of his taints are utterly destroyed.
This person is called one who has attained through vision.
And what is the person liberated by faith?
Here, a certain person understands as it really is: "This is suffering" ... [and so on] ... [as in the standard formula].
“He understands as it really is: ‘This is the practice leading to the cessation of suffering.

The teachings proclaimed by the Tathāgata have been clearly seen and mastered by him through wisdom; having seen with wisdom, some of his taints are utterly destroyed, though not to the same extent as that of one who has attained through vision.”
This person is called one liberated by faith.
And what kind of person is a follower by Dhamma?

It is the person who, while practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, possesses a predominant faculty of wisdom and develops the Noble Path with wisdom as its vehicle and wisdom as its precursor.
This person is called one who follows the Dhamma.
A person practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry is one who follows the Dhamma; established in the fruit, they are one who has attained vision.
And what is a person who follows by faith?

The person who has entered upon the practice for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry and whose faculty of faith is predominant develops the Noble Path, which is carried by faith and preceded by faith.
Such a person is called a "follower by faith" (saddhānusārī).
A person practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry is a follower by faith; one established in the fruit is "liberated by faith" (saddhāvimutta).
The Exposition of the Nines.
